14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
69: 
70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
72: 
73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95: 
96: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
97: 
98: ```markdown
99: # Git Commit Workflows
100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
104: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
118: ```
119: 
120: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
121: 
122: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
123: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
124: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
125: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
126: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
127: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
128: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
129: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
130: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ### Reference Body Skeleton
135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
137: 
138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166: 
167: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
172: 
173: ### [Rule Group]
174: 
175: - **Rule:** [What to do]
176: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
177: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
182: 
183: [Body of the section]
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
188: 
189: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
190: ```
191: 
192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
194: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
195: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
196: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
197: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
198: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.
199: 
200: ---

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES
235: 
236: ### Create Reference File When
237: 
238: **Workflow Complexity**:
239: - Multi-phase workflows with validation checkpoints
240: - Decision trees with multiple branches
241: - Pattern libraries with 5+ variations
242: - Systematic debugging procedures
243: 
244: **Technical Depth**:
245: - Root cause analysis required
246: - Tool integration details (MCP, scripts)
247: - Before/after code transformations
248: - Common error patterns and fixes
249: 
250: **Size Threshold**:
251: - Content exceeds 200 lines
252: - Multiple related workflows
253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed
254: 
255: ### Keep in SKILL.md When
256: 
257: **Core Content**:
258: - Overview and "When to Use"
259: - High-level workflow (3-5 steps)
260: - Essential rules (ALWAYS/NEVER/ESCALATE IF)
261:   > **Note**: RULES sections in SKILL.md use ALL-CAPS H3 headers: `### ALWAYS`, `### NEVER`, `### ESCALATE IF` (or `####` at phase depth). See [skill-md-template.md](./skill-md-template.md) for the complete pattern.
262: - Quick reference
263: 
264: **Size**: Content under 200 lines
265: 
266: ### Reference File Types for AI Agent Skills
267: 
268: | Type                | Purpose                                | Example (kebab-case)          | Size           |
269: | ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------- |
270: | **Workflow**        | Multi-phase processes with checkpoints | `implementation-workflows.md` | 500-1500 lines |
271: | **Pattern Library** | Code patterns with before/after        | `shared-patterns.md`          | 300-800 lines  |
272: | **Standards**       | Rules and conventions                  | `code-quality-standards.md`   | 400-1000 lines |
273: | **Debugging**       | Systematic troubleshooting             | `debugging-workflows.md`      | 600-1200 lines |
274: | **Tool Guide**      | MCP/external tool integration          | `devtools-guide.md`           | 200-600 lines  |
275: | **Quick Reference** | Commands, shortcuts, checklists        | `quick-reference.md`          | 200-400 lines  |
276: 
277: **Note:** All authored reference file names use kebab-case (hyphens, lowercase).
278: 
279: ---

281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284: 
285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
286: 
287: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
288: 
289: **Format**:
290: ```markdown
291: \## 1. OVERVIEW
292: 
293: ### Purpose
294: 
295: [The outcome this reference produces]
296: 
297: ### When to Use
298: 
299: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
300: 
301: ### Core Principle
302: 
303: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
304: ```
305: 
306: **Examples from Real Skills**:
307: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
308: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
309: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
310: 
311: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
312: 
313: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
314: 
315: **Format**:
316: ```markdown
317: ### The [Number] Phases
318: 
319: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.

322: 
323: **Purpose**: [What this phase accomplishes]

328: 
329: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`

331: #### Phase 2: [Phase Name]
332: 
333: [Similar structure]
334: ```

336: **Key Elements**:
337: - **"You MUST complete"** - Mandatory language
338: - **Named checkpoints** - `checkpoint_name` for validation

342: 
343: **Purpose**: Show transformation from wrong to right

348:

361: **Why better**: [Explanation of improvement]
362: ```
363: 
364: **Key Elements**:
365: - `BEFORE:` marker for the wrong-way code
366: - `AFTER:` marker for the right-way code
367: - Inline comments explaining issues
368: - "Why better" rationale

372: **Purpose**: Compare approaches across scenarios

381: | [Scenario 2] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766: 
767: ---
768: 
769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"
1073:

21: 
22: ### Location & Naming

25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only

38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.

70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.

73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95:

98: ```markdown

100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!

105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes

109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!

193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.

245: - Root cause analysis required

253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed

262: - Quick reference

264: **Size**: Content under 200 lines

281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284: 
285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
286: 
287: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
288: 
289: **Format**:
290: ```markdown
291: \## 1. OVERVIEW
292: 
293: ### Purpose
294: 
295: [The outcome this reference produces]
296: 
297: ### When to Use
298: 
299: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
300: 
301: ### Core Principle
302: 
303: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
304: ```
305: 
306: **Examples from Real Skills**:
307: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
308: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
309: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
310: 
311: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
312: 
313: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
314: 
315: **Format**:
316: ```markdown
317: ### The [Number] Phases
318: 
319: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
320: 
321: #### Phase 1: [Phase Name]
322: 
323: **Purpose**: [What this phase accomplishes]
324: 
325: **Actions**:
326: 1. [Action 1]
327: 2. [Action 2]
328: 
329: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`

332: 
333: [Similar structure]
334: ```

337: - **"You MUST complete"** - Mandatory language
338: - **Named checkpoints** - `checkpoint_name` for validation
339: - **Sequential phases** - Cannot skip ahead

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766:

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882:

884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006:

1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"

1: ---
2: title: "Obsidian CLI Reference"
3: description: "Complete command reference for both Obsidian CLI profiles: notesmd-cli (headless, filesystem) and the official obsidian CLI (app-backed remote control), with usage, flags, and agent patterns."
4: trigger_phrases:
5:   - "notesmd-cli commands"
6:   - "obsidian cli"
7:   - "notesmd-cli create"
8:   - "notesmd-cli search"
9:   - "obsidian daily note"
10:   - "obsidian vault cli"
11: importance_tier: "normal"
12: contextType: "implementation"
13: version: 0.2.0.0
14: ---
15: 
16: # Obsidian CLI Reference
17: 
18: Two distinct CLI profiles operate an Obsidian vault. Pick by whether a live app is available.
19: 
20: - **`notesmd-cli`** (Yakitrak) — HEADLESS. Operates directly on the vault filesystem. Works with **no running Obsidian app**. This is the default for agent automation.
21: - **`obsidian`** (official) — APP-BACKED. A remote control for an already-running Obsidian desktop app. It does **not** launch the app, and fails with exit 1 when the app is down. Not headless.
22: 
23: ---
24: 
25: ## 1. OVERVIEW
26: 
27: `notesmd-cli` is a Go CLI that reads and writes the vault's markdown files directly. Because it never talks to a running app, it is the reliable surface for scripted, headless agent workflows: create notes, search content, list files, edit frontmatter, and manage which vault is the default — all against the filesystem.
28: 
29: The official `obsidian` CLI is a thin remote control shipped inside the desktop app (GA in desktop v1.12.4, Feb 2026). It drives an app that is **already running** and does not start one. It is the right surface when you need the live app's resolved link graph, its computed tag/task index, its plugins, sync and file history, or its rendering. Agent-facing usage, preflight and the exit-0 failure contract: [`official-cli-agent-usage.md`](official-cli-agent-usage.md).
30: 
31: **Key agent advantages of `notesmd-cli`:**
32: - No app dependency — runs on servers, in CI, over SSH
33: - Operates on plain files — deterministic, greppable, diff-able
34: - Multi-vault aware — `add-vault` / `set-default-vault` route commands to the right vault
35: 
36: > The binary is named `notesmd-cli` (renamed from "obsidian-cli" to avoid confusion with the official CLI). Do not invoke it as `obsidian-cli`.
37: 
38: ---
39: 
40: ## 2. PREREQUISITES
41: 
42: **`notesmd-cli` (headless):**
43: - Installed: `notesmd-cli --version` `VERIFY exact version-flag output`
44: - At least one vault registered: `notesmd-cli list-vaults`
45: - A default vault set: `notesmd-cli set-default-vault <name>`
46: 
47: **Install `notesmd-cli`:**
48: ```bash
49: # macOS / Linux (Homebrew)
50: brew tap yakitrak/yakitrak && brew install yakitrak/yakitrak/notesmd-cli
51: 
52: # Windows (Scoop)
53: scoop bucket add scoop-yakitrak https://github.com/yakitrak/scoop-yakitrak.git
54: scoop install notesmd-cli
55: 
56: # Arch (AUR)
57: yay -S notesmd-cli-bin
58: 
59: # From source (Go 1.19+) — clone + `go build`; NOTE: `go install` is not supported
60: ```
61: 
62: **`obsidian` (official, app-backed):**
63: - Obsidian desktop **v1.12.4+** installed
64: - Enable in-app: **Settings → General → Command line interface → toggle on → "Register CLI"** (auto-adds `obsidian` to PATH on mac/Linux)
65: - Obsidian must be installed/registered **and the desktop app must already be running**; the CLI does not launch it (confirmed: exit 1 with `The CLI is unable to find Obsidian` when the app is down)
66: 
67: ---
68: 
69: ## 3. PROFILE SELECTION (notesmd-cli vs official obsidian)
70: 
71: | Need | Use | Reason |
72: |------|-----|--------|
73: | Create/edit/search notes with no app running | `notesmd-cli` | Filesystem-native, headless |
74: | Scripted / CI / server automation | `notesmd-cli` | No GUI dependency |
75: | Manage multiple vaults, set default | `notesmd-cli` | `add-vault`/`set-default-vault` |
76: | Anything against a running app that is not section-scoped editing or tag writing | `obsidian` | The default app-backed surface. 106 commands, app-only prerequisite |
77: | Drive the live app (open a note in the running UI) | `obsidian` | App-backed remote control |
78: | Resolved link graph: backlinks, orphans, unresolved | `obsidian` | Only the running app holds the resolved graph |
79: | Vault-wide tags, tasks or properties as the app computes them | `obsidian` | The index lives in the app, not in the files |
80: | Bases queries, sync history, file version history | `obsidian` | No filesystem equivalent |
81: | Plugin, theme or snippet state changes | `obsidian` | Mutates live app state |
82: 
83: > **Agent default:** prefer `notesmd-cli`. When the outcome requires the running app, the official `obsidian` CLI is the default app-backed surface, ahead of the MCP server. Escalate to MCP only for in-place section patching, in-note search-and-replace, tag-list writes, JSON-typed frontmatter, or a batch over roughly 20 calls. Measured comparison: [`cli-versus-mcp.md`](cli-versus-mcp.md).
84: 
85: ---
86: 
87: ## 4. VAULT CONFIGURATION (notesmd-cli)
88: 
89: | Command | Description | Example |
90: |---------|-------------|---------|
91: | `notesmd-cli add-vault <path>` | Register a vault by filesystem path | `notesmd-cli add-vault ~/Notes` |
92: | `notesmd-cli add-vault <path> --name <name>` | Register with an explicit name `VERIFY flag` | `notesmd-cli add-vault ~/Notes --name work` |
93: | `notesmd-cli remove-vault <name>` | Unregister a vault | `notesmd-cli remove-vault work` |
94: | `notesmd-cli list-vaults` | List registered vaults | `notesmd-cli list-vaults` |
95: | `notesmd-cli set-default-vault <name>` | Set the vault used when `--vault` is omitted | `notesmd-cli set-default-vault work` |
96: 
97: **Config storage:** vault registrations live at `~/.config/obsidian/obsidian.json`.
98: 
99: **Agent pattern:** always confirm the target vault before a write.
100: ```bash
101: notesmd-cli list-vaults              # See registered vaults + which is default
102: notesmd-cli set-default-vault work   # Pin the vault this session will operate on
103: ```
104: 
105: ---
106: 
107: ## 5. NOTE READING & LISTING (notesmd-cli)
108: 
109: | Command | Description | Notes |
110: |---------|-------------|-------|
111: | `notesmd-cli list` | List notes in the (default) vault | Add `--vault <name>` to target another |
112: | `notesmd-cli print <note>` | Print a note's contents to stdout | Machine-readable; safe to pipe |
113: | `notesmd-cli search <query>` | Search note **titles/names** for a term | **Broken in v0.3.6 (validated):** returns "Cannot find note in vault" even for on-disk notes. Use `list` + filter or `search-content` for name lookups. |
114: | `notesmd-cli search-content <query>` | Full-text search across note **bodies** | Slower; scans file contents |
115: 
116: **Agent pattern — read before you write:**
117: ```bash
118: notesmd-cli list | grep -i "Sprint"   # Find notes by name — notesmd-cli search (title) is broken in v0.3.6
119: notesmd-cli search-content "blocker"  # Find notes mentioning a term in the body (reliable)
120: notesmd-cli print "Sprint Board"      # Read the full note before editing
121: ```
122: 
123: ---
124: 
125: ## 6. NOTE CREATION & MUTATION (notesmd-cli)
126: 
127: | Command | Description | Notes |
128: |---------|-------------|-------|
129: | `notesmd-cli create <note>` | Create a new note | `VERIFY` flags for content/body input (e.g. `--content`, stdin, or open-in-editor) |
130: | `notesmd-cli open <note>` | Open a note | Headless: resolves/prints the note `VERIFY`; app-backed open is the official CLI's job |
131: | `notesmd-cli daily` | Create/open today's daily note | Honors the vault's daily-note settings `VERIFY` |
132: | `notesmd-cli move <src> <dst>` | Move/rename a note (updates links) `VERIFY link-update` | Prefer over raw `mv` so backlinks follow |
133: | `notesmd-cli delete <note>` | Delete a note | Destructive — see agent invariants (§11) |
134: | `notesmd-cli frontmatter <note>` | Read/modify a note's YAML frontmatter | `VERIFY` get-vs-set flag surface |
135: 
136: > **`VERIFY` note:** exact flags for `create` (how body content is supplied) and `frontmatter` (read vs. set, key/value syntax) are not confirmed in this pass. Run `notesmd-cli <command> --help` against the installed binary to confirm before scripting bulk writes.
137: 
138: **Agent pattern — safe create:**
139: ```bash
140: notesmd-cli search "Meeting 2026-08-02"       # Confirm it does not already exist
141: notesmd-cli create "Meeting 2026-08-02"       # Create it (VERIFY content-input flag)
142: notesmd-cli print "Meeting 2026-08-02"        # Read back to confirm
143: ```
144: 
145: ---
146: 
147: ## 7. FULL SUBCOMMAND INVENTORY (notesmd-cli)
148: 
149: Fourteen subcommands, grouped by purpose:
150: 
151: | Group | Subcommands |
152: |-------|-------------|
153: | Read | `list`, `print`, `search`, `search-content` |
154: | Write | `create`, `daily`, `move`, `delete`, `frontmatter` |
155: | Navigate | `open` |
156: | Vault config | `add-vault`, `remove-vault`, `list-vaults`, `set-default-vault` |
157: 
158: > **Headless note:** every subcommand above operates on the vault **filesystem** and needs **no running Obsidian app**. This is what makes `notesmd-cli` safe for servers, CI, and unattended agent runs. Behavior that requires the live app (rendering, plugin execution, UI focus) is out of scope for `notesmd-cli` — use the official `obsidian` CLI (§8) for that.
159: 
160: ---
161: 
162: ## 8. OFFICIAL OBSIDIAN CLI (APP-BACKED)
163: 
164: The official `obsidian` binary ships inside Obsidian desktop **v1.12.4+** and is a remote control for a running app. It is **not** headless, and it does **not** start the app: with the app down every invocation prints `The CLI is unable to find Obsidian. Please make sure Obsidian is running and try again.` to stderr and exits 1.
165: 
166: **Enable it (one-time):** Settings → General → Command line interface → toggle on → **"Register CLI"**. On macOS/Linux this registers `obsidian` on PATH; the app must be installed.
167: 
168: **Syntax:** `obsidian <command> key=value`. The subcommands are `obsidian version` and `obsidian help`. POSIX flags are not the grammar: `obsidian --version`, `-v` and `-h` each print `Error: Command "..." not found.` and still exit 0. The one exception measured on 1.13.7 is `obsidian --help`, whose output is byte-identical to `obsidian help`. Do not rely on it, since it is undocumented.
169: 
170: **Command surface:** 106 commands, confirmed against desktop 1.13.7 (installer 1.13.4). `obsidian help` prints the authoritative list.
171: 
172: | Capability | Status | Notes |
173: |------------|--------|-------|
174: | Read, create, append, prepend, delete, move, rename notes | Confirmed | `obsidian read file="Note"`, `obsidian create name="Note" content="..."`. There is no patch or in-note replace command |
175: | Search the vault | Confirmed | `search` and `search:context`, both with `format=json` |
176: | Resolved link graph | Confirmed present | `backlinks`, `links`, `orphans`, `deadends`, `unresolved` — no filesystem equivalent |
177: | Vault-wide tags, tasks, properties | Confirmed present | `tags`, `tasks`, `properties`, `property:set` / `property:read` / `property:remove`. `tag` and `tags` are **read-only**: the CLI cannot add or remove a tag |
178: | Bases queries, sync and file history | Confirmed present | `base:query`, `sync:*`, `history:*`, `diff` |
179: | Plugin, theme and snippet control | Confirmed present | `plugin:enable`, `theme:set`, `snippet:enable` and siblings |
180: | Arbitrary JavaScript in the live app | Confirmed | `eval code="..."` returns `=> <result>`. Not sandboxed |
181: | Launch the app if not running | **Not supported** | The CLI fails with exit 1 and leaves the app down |
182: | Headless file operations | Not supported | Use `notesmd-cli` — the official CLI requires the running app |
183: 
184: > **Two contracts an agent must respect before scripting this CLI.** First, run the preflight: `obsidian version` prints a version number only when the binary is registered **and** the app is answering. Test the output, not the status, because an app that is still starting answers 0 with an error on stdout. Second, once the app is up the CLI **exits 0 even on failure** and prints `Error: ...` to stdout, so `$?` is not a success signal. Both, with the command surface and the safety invariants, are in [`official-cli-agent-usage.md`](official-cli-agent-usage.md).
185: 
186: **When to prefer it:** whenever the outcome requires the live app. That covers the resolved link graph, the computed tag and task index, Bases, sync and file history, plugin and theme state, and the UI itself, none of which the MCP server exposes. For everything file-shaped, `notesmd-cli` is faster and needs no app. Where the CLI and the MCP server overlap, the CLI wins the default on prerequisites and coverage, and loses only on in-place section editing, tag writes and warm-batch latency. See [`cli-versus-mcp.md`](cli-versus-mcp.md).
187: 
188: ---
189: 
190: ## 9. GLOBAL FLAGS (notesmd-cli)
191: 
192: > The official `obsidian` CLI has no POSIX flags. Its one global option is `vault=<name>`, accepted either before or after the command word.
193: 
194: 
195: | Flag | Applies To | Description |
196: |------|-----------|-------------|
197: | `--vault <name>` | Most commands | Target a specific registered vault instead of the default `VERIFY flag name` |
198: | `--help` / `-h` | All | Print usage for the command (authoritative source for exact flags) |
199: | `--version` | — | Print `notesmd-cli` version `VERIFY exact spelling` |
200: 
201: > When in doubt about a flag, `notesmd-cli <command> --help` on the installed binary is authoritative — this document marks unconfirmed specifics `VERIFY` rather than guessing.
202: 
203: ---
204: 
205: ## 10. HEADLESS WORKFLOW RECIPES (notesmd-cli)
206: 
207: **Create a dated note, then read it back:**
208: ```bash
209: notesmd-cli create "Standup $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)"
210: notesmd-cli print  "Standup $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)"
211: ```
212: 
213: **Find notes touching a topic, across titles and bodies:**
214: ```bash
215: notesmd-cli search "roadmap"            # Title-level
216: notesmd-cli search-content "roadmap"    # Body-level (full-text)
217: ```
218: 
219: **Open (or create) today's daily note:**
220: ```bash
221: notesmd-cli daily
222: ```
223: 
224: **Rename a note so backlinks follow:**
225: ```bash
226: notesmd-cli move "Draft" "Published/Launch Plan"   # Prefer over raw mv (VERIFY link-update)
227: ```
228: 
229: ---
230: 
231: ## 11. AGENT INVARIANTS (MUST FOLLOW)
232: 
233: ### 1. Confirm the vault before writing
234: 
235: ```bash
236: # WRONG — assume the default vault is the intended one:
237: notesmd-cli create "Important Note"
238: 
239: # RIGHT — verify which vault is default first:
240: notesmd-cli list-vaults                  # Which vault is default?
241: notesmd-cli set-default-vault work       # Pin it explicitly for this session

2: title: "Obsidian CLI Reference"
3: description: "Complete command reference for both Obsidian CLI profiles: notesmd-cli (headless, filesystem) and the official obsidian CLI (app-backed remote control), with usage, flags, and agent patterns."
4: trigger_phrases:
5:   - "notesmd-cli commands"
6:   - "obsidian cli"
7:   - "notesmd-cli create"
8:   - "notesmd-cli search"

13: version: 0.2.0.0
14: ---
15: 
16: # Obsidian CLI Reference
17: 
18: Two distinct CLI profiles operate an Obsidian vault. Pick by whether a live app is available.
19: 
20: - **`notesmd-cli`** (Yakitrak) — HEADLESS. Operates directly on the vault filesystem. Works with **no running Obsidian app**. This is the default for agent automation.
21: - **`obsidian`** (official) — APP-BACKED. A remote control for an already-running Obsidian desktop app. It does **not** launch the app, and fails with exit 1 when the app is down. Not headless.
22: 
23: ---
24: 
25: ## 1. OVERVIEW
26: 
27: `notesmd-cli` is a Go CLI that reads and writes the vault's markdown files directly. Because it never talks to a running app, it is the reliable surface for scripted, headless agent workflows: create notes, search content, list files, edit frontmatter, and manage which vault is the default — all against the filesystem.
28: 
29: The official `obsidian` CLI is a thin remote control shipped inside the desktop app (GA in desktop v1.12.4, Feb 2026). It drives an app that is **already running** and does not start one. It is the right surface when you need the live app's resolved link graph, its computed tag/task index, its plugins, sync and file history, or its rendering. Agent-facing usage, preflight and the exit-0 failure contract: [`official-cli-agent-usage.md`](official-cli-agent-usage.md).
30: 
31: **Key agent advantages of `notesmd-cli`:**
32: - No app dependency — runs on servers, in CI, over SSH
33: - Operates on plain files — deterministic, greppable, diff-able
34: - Multi-vault aware — `add-vault` / `set-default-vault` route commands to the right vault
35: 
36: > The binary is named `notesmd-cli` (renamed from "obsidian-cli" to avoid confusion with the official CLI). Do not invoke it as `obsidian-cli`.
37: 
38: ---
39: 
40: ## 2. PREREQUISITES
41: 
42: **`notesmd-cli` (headless):**
43: - Installed: `notesmd-cli --version` `VERIFY exact version-flag output`
44: - At least one vault registered: `notesmd-cli list-vaults`
45: - A default vault set: `notesmd-cli set-default-vault <name>`
46: 
47: **Install `notesmd-cli`:**
48: ```bash
49: # macOS / Linux (Homebrew)
50: brew tap yakitrak/yakitrak && brew install yakitrak/yakitrak/notesmd-cli
51: 
52: # Windows (Scoop)
53: scoop bucket add scoop-yakitrak https://github.com/yakitrak/scoop-yakitrak.git
54: scoop install notesmd-cli
55: 
56: # Arch (AUR)
57: yay -S notesmd-cli-bin
58: 
59: # From source (Go 1.19+) — clone + `go build`; NOTE: `go install` is not supported
60: ```
61: 
62: **`obsidian` (official, app-backed):**
63: - Obsidian desktop **v1.12.4+** installed
64: - Enable in-app: **Settings → General → Command line interface → toggle on → "Register CLI"** (auto-adds `obsidian` to PATH on mac/Linux)
65: - Obsidian must be installed/registered **and the desktop app must already be running**; the CLI does not launch it (confirmed: exit 1 with `The CLI is unable to find Obsidian` when the app is down)
66: 
67: ---
68: 
69: ## 3. PROFILE SELECTION (notesmd-cli vs official obsidian)
70: 
71: | Need | Use | Reason |
72: |------|-----|--------|
73: | Create/edit/search notes with no app running | `notesmd-cli` | Filesystem-native, headless |
74: | Scripted / CI / server automation | `notesmd-cli` | No GUI dependency |
75: | Manage multiple vaults, set default | `notesmd-cli` | `add-vault`/`set-default-vault` |
76: | Anything against a running app that is not section-scoped editing or tag writing | `obsidian` | The default app-backed surface. 106 commands, app-only prerequisite |
77: | Drive the live app (open a note in the running UI) | `obsidian` | App-backed remote control |
78: | Resolved link graph: backlinks, orphans, unresolved | `obsidian` | Only the running app holds the resolved graph |
79: | Vault-wide tags, tasks or properties as the app computes them | `obsidian` | The index lives in the app, not in the files |
80: | Bases queries, sync history, file version history | `obsidian` | No filesystem equivalent |
81: | Plugin, theme or snippet state changes | `obsidian` | Mutates live app state |
82: 
83: > **Agent default:** prefer `notesmd-cli`. When the outcome requires the running app, the official `obsidian` CLI is the default app-backed surface, ahead of the MCP server. Escalate to MCP only for in-place section patching, in-note search-and-replace, tag-list writes, JSON-typed frontmatter, or a batch over roughly 20 calls. Measured comparison: [`cli-versus-mcp.md`](cli-versus-mcp.md).
84: 
85: ---
86: 
87: ## 4. VAULT CONFIGURATION (notesmd-cli)
88: 
89: | Command | Description | Example |
90: |---------|-------------|---------|
91: | `notesmd-cli add-vault <path>` | Register a vault by filesystem path | `notesmd-cli add-vault ~/Notes` |
92: | `notesmd-cli add-vault <path> --name <name>` | Register with an explicit name `VERIFY flag` | `notesmd-cli add-vault ~/Notes --name work` |
93: | `notesmd-cli remove-vault <name>` | Unregister a vault | `notesmd-cli remove-vault work` |
94: | `notesmd-cli list-vaults` | List registered vaults | `notesmd-cli list-vaults` |
95: | `notesmd-cli set-default-vault <name>` | Set the vault used when `--vault` is omitted | `notesmd-cli set-default-vault work` |
96: 
97: **Config storage:** vault registrations live at `~/.config/obsidian/obsidian.json`.
98: 
99: **Agent pattern:** always confirm the target vault before a write.
100: ```bash
101: notesmd-cli list-vaults              # See registered vaults + which is default
102: notesmd-cli set-default-vault work   # Pin the vault this session will operate on
103: ```
104: 
105: ---
106: 
107: ## 5. NOTE READING & LISTING (notesmd-cli)
108: 
109: | Command | Description | Notes |
110: |---------|-------------|-------|
111: | `notesmd-cli list` | List notes in the (default) vault | Add `--vault <name>` to target another |
112: | `notesmd-cli print <note>` | Print a note's contents to stdout | Machine-readable; safe to pipe |
113: | `notesmd-cli search <query>` | Search note **titles/names** for a term | **Broken in v0.3.6 (validated):** returns "Cannot find note in vault" even for on-disk notes. Use `list` + filter or `search-content` for name lookups. |
114: | `notesmd-cli search-content <query>` | Full-text search across note **bodies** | Slower; scans file contents |
115: 
116: **Agent pattern — read before you write:**
117: ```bash
118: notesmd-cli list | grep -i "Sprint"   # Find notes by name — notesmd-cli search (title) is broken in v0.3.6
119: notesmd-cli search-content "blocker"  # Find notes mentioning a term in the body (reliable)
120: notesmd-cli print "Sprint Board"      # Read the full note before editing
121: ```
122: 
123: ---
124: 
125: ## 6. NOTE CREATION & MUTATION (notesmd-cli)
126: 
127: | Command | Description | Notes |
128: |---------|-------------|-------|
129: | `notesmd-cli create <note>` | Create a new note | `VERIFY` flags for content/body input (e.g. `--content`, stdin, or open-in-editor) |
130: | `notesmd-cli open <note>` | Open a note | Headless: resolves/prints the note `VERIFY`; app-backed open is the official CLI's job |
131: | `notesmd-cli daily` | Create/open today's daily note | Honors the vault's daily-note settings `VERIFY` |
132: | `notesmd-cli move <src> <dst>` | Move/rename a note (updates links) `VERIFY link-update` | Prefer over raw `mv` so backlinks follow |
133: | `notesmd-cli delete <note>` | Delete a note | Destructive — see agent invariants (§11) |
134: | `notesmd-cli frontmatter <note>` | Read/modify a note's YAML frontmatter | `VERIFY` get-vs-set flag surface |
135: 
136: > **`VERIFY` note:** exact flags for `create` (how body content is supplied) and `frontmatter` (read vs. set, key/value syntax) are not confirmed in this pass. Run `notesmd-cli <command> --help` against the installed binary to confirm before scripting bulk writes.
137: 
138: **Agent pattern — safe create:**
139: ```bash
140: notesmd-cli search "Meeting 2026-08-02"       # Confirm it does not already exist
141: notesmd-cli create "Meeting 2026-08-02"       # Create it (VERIFY content-input flag)
142: notesmd-cli print "Meeting 2026-08-02"        # Read back to confirm
143: ```
144: 
145: ---
146: 
147: ## 7. FULL SUBCOMMAND INVENTORY (notesmd-cli)
148: 
149: Fourteen subcommands, grouped by purpose:
150: 
151: | Group | Subcommands |
152: |-------|-------------|
153: | Read | `list`, `print`, `search`, `search-content` |
154: | Write | `create`, `daily`, `move`, `delete`, `frontmatter` |
155: | Navigate | `open` |
156: | Vault config | `add-vault`, `remove-vault`, `list-vaults`, `set-default-vault` |
157: 
158: > **Headless note:** every subcommand above operates on the vault **filesystem** and needs **no running Obsidian app**. This is what makes `notesmd-cli` safe for servers, CI, and unattended agent runs. Behavior that requires the live app (rendering, plugin execution, UI focus) is out of scope for `notesmd-cli` — use the official `obsidian` CLI (§8) for that.
159: 
160: ---
161: 
162: ## 8. OFFICIAL OBSIDIAN CLI (APP-BACKED)
163: 
164: The official `obsidian` binary ships inside Obsidian desktop **v1.12.4+** and is a remote control for a running app. It is **not** headless, and it does **not** start the app: with the app down every invocation prints `The CLI is unable to find Obsidian. Please make sure Obsidian is running and try again.` to stderr and exits 1.
165: 
166: **Enable it (one-time):** Settings → General → Command line interface → toggle on → **"Register CLI"**. On macOS/Linux this registers `obsidian` on PATH; the app must be installed.
167: 
168: **Syntax:** `obsidian <command> key=value`. The subcommands are `obsidian version` and `obsidian help`. POSIX flags are not the grammar: `obsidian --version`, `-v` and `-h` each print `Error: Command "..." not found.` and still exit 0. The one exception measured on 1.13.7 is `obsidian --help`, whose output is byte-identical to `obsidian help`. Do not rely on it, since it is undocumented.
169: 
170: **Command surface:** 106 commands, confirmed against desktop 1.13.7 (installer 1.13.4). `obsidian help` prints the authoritative list.
171: 
172: | Capability | Status | Notes |
173: |------------|--------|-------|
174: | Read, create, append, prepend, delete, move, rename notes | Confirmed | `obsidian read file="Note"`, `obsidian create name="Note" content="..."`. There is no patch or in-note replace command |
175: | Search the vault | Confirmed | `search` and `search:context`, both with `format=json` |
176: | Resolved link graph | Confirmed present | `backlinks`, `links`, `orphans`, `deadends`, `unresolved` — no filesystem equivalent |
177: | Vault-wide tags, tasks, properties | Confirmed present | `tags`, `tasks`, `properties`, `property:set` / `property:read` / `property:remove`. `tag` and `tags` are **read-only**: the CLI cannot add or remove a tag |
178: | Bases queries, sync and file history | Confirmed present | `base:query`, `sync:*`, `history:*`, `diff` |
179: | Plugin, theme and snippet control | Confirmed present | `plugin:enable`, `theme:set`, `snippet:enable` and siblings |
180: | Arbitrary JavaScript in the live app | Confirmed | `eval code="..."` returns `=> <result>`. Not sandboxed |
181: | Launch the app if not running | **Not supported** | The CLI fails with exit 1 and leaves the app down |
182: | Headless file operations | Not supported | Use `notesmd-cli` — the official CLI requires the running app |
183: 
184: > **Two contracts an agent must respect before scripting this CLI.** First, run the preflight: `obsidian version` prints a version number only when the binary is registered **and** the app is answering. Test the output, not the status, because an app that is still starting answers 0 with an error on stdout. Second, once the app is up the CLI **exits 0 even on failure** and prints `Error: ...` to stdout, so `$?` is not a success signal. Both, with the command surface and the safety invariants, are in [`official-cli-agent-usage.md`](official-cli-agent-usage.md).
185: 
186: **When to prefer it:** whenever the outcome requires the live app. That covers the resolved link graph, the computed tag and task index, Bases, sync and file history, plugin and theme state, and the UI itself, none of which the MCP server exposes. For everything file-shaped, `notesmd-cli` is faster and needs no app. Where the CLI and the MCP server overlap, the CLI wins the default on prerequisites and coverage, and loses only on in-place section editing, tag writes and warm-batch latency. See [`cli-versus-mcp.md`](cli-versus-mcp.md).
187: 
188: ---
189: 
190: ## 9. GLOBAL FLAGS (notesmd-cli)
191: 
192: > The official `obsidian` CLI has no POSIX flags. Its one global option is `vault=<name>`, accepted either before or after the command word.
193: 
194: 
195: | Flag | Applies To | Description |
196: |------|-----------|-------------|
197: | `--vault <name>` | Most commands | Target a specific registered vault instead of the default `VERIFY flag name` |
198: | `--help` / `-h` | All | Print usage for the command (authoritative source for exact flags) |
199: | `--version` | — | Print `notesmd-cli` version `VERIFY exact spelling` |
200: 
201: > When in doubt about a flag, `notesmd-cli <command> --help` on the installed binary is authoritative — this document marks unconfirmed specifics `VERIFY` rather than guessing.
202: 
203: ---
204: 
205: ## 10. HEADLESS WORKFLOW RECIPES (notesmd-cli)
206: 
207: **Create a dated note, then read it back:**
208: ```bash
209: notesmd-cli create "Standup $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)"
210: notesmd-cli print  "Standup $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)"
211: ```
212: 
213: **Find notes touching a topic, across titles and bodies:**
214: ```bash
215: notesmd-cli search "roadmap"            # Title-level
216: notesmd-cli search-content "roadmap"    # Body-level (full-text)
217: ```
218: 
219: **Open (or create) today's daily note:**
220: ```bash
221: notesmd-cli daily
222: ```
223: 
224: **Rename a note so backlinks follow:**
225: ```bash
226: notesmd-cli move "Draft" "Published/Launch Plan"   # Prefer over raw mv (VERIFY link-update)
227: ```
228: 
229: ---
230: 
231: ## 11. AGENT INVARIANTS (MUST FOLLOW)
232: 
233: ### 1. Confirm the vault before writing
234: 
235: ```bash
236: # WRONG — assume the default vault is the intended one:
237: notesmd-cli create "Important Note"
238: 
239: # RIGHT — verify which vault is default first:
240: notesmd-cli list-vaults                  # Which vault is default?
241: notesmd-cli set-default-vault work       # Pin it explicitly for this session
242: notesmd-cli create "Important Note"
243: ```
244: 
245: ### 2. Read before mutate
246: 
247: ```bash
248: notesmd-cli search "Sprint Board"        # Does it exist?
249: notesmd-cli print  "Sprint Board"        # Read current contents
250: # THEN edit / move / delete
251: ```
252: 
253: ### 3. Delete and move are destructive — confirm the target
254: 
255: ```bash
256: # WRONG — delete on an unverified name:
257: notesmd-cli delete "Notes"               # Ambiguous — which note?
258: 
259: # RIGHT — resolve the exact note first:
260: notesmd-cli search "Notes"               # Confirm the exact title
261: notesmd-cli print  "Notes/2026-08-02"    # Confirm it is the right file
262: notesmd-cli delete "Notes/2026-08-02"
263: ```
264: 
265: ### 4. Empty search result is VALID
266: 
267: ```bash
268: # An empty result means no matching note exists — not an error.
269: result="$(notesmd-cli search "nonexistent" || true)"
270: if [[ -z "$result" ]]; then
271:   echo "No matching note. Not fabricating one."
272:   # Before escalating: try search-content, check the vault, verify spelling.
273:   notesmd-cli search-content "nonexistent"

275: fi
276: ```
277: 
278: ### 5. Prefer notesmd-cli; escalate to the official CLI only for app-only outcomes
279:

Reach for it only when the result requires the live app (§8), and before depending on it run the preflight `obsidian version` and check its output looks like a version — exit 0 means the binary is registered and the app is up. Once the app is running the CLI **exits 0 on failure**, so check its stdout for a leading `Error:` rather than `$?`. Full contract: [`official-cli-agent-usage.md`](official-cli-agent-usage.md).
281: 
282: ---
283: 
284: ## 12. CONFIGURATION STORAGE
285: 
286: | Profile | Config location |
287: |---------|-----------------|
288: | `notesmd-cli` | Vault registrations at `~/.config/obsidian/obsidian.json` |
289: | `obsidian` (official) | Managed in-app (Settings → General → Command line interface). On macOS registration symlinks `/usr/local/bin/obsidian` into the app bundle; no separate CLI config file |
